audit_findings.title: Nonrecourse securitization cash may be attributed to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 exposure: $32.164m of securitized-intangible amortization versus $29.493m of bond-principal repayment and only $0.145m of KGSS-I net income; $32.164m equals 12.6% of the $255.5m anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is overstated if ring-fenced intangible amortization is added back without deducting the associated customer-charge cash committed to bond principal and debt service.
audit_findings.evidence: KGSS-I’s assets cannot be used to settle ONE Gas’ obligations and the holders of the Securitized Utility Tariff Bonds have no recourse against ONE Gas.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that KGSS-I is nonrecourse and that its revenues, amortization, interest, and principal runoff are substantial but nearly neutral to consolidated earnings. It does not demonstrate how the OE workpaper treated these items. If the $32.164m amortization was added back without the matching restricted cash use, the recurring distortion is large enough to affect the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile KGSS-I customer charges, operating costs, interest, intangible amortization, restricted-cash changes, and bond-principal repayments for every OE year; rerun all scenarios after limiting KGSS-I's contribution to cash economically available to common equity.

audit_findings.title: Assumed growth may belong partly to future shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $204.4m of unused ATM capacity at June 30, 2026; resulting future share dilution and value transfer are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Projected total-company OE growth is divided by a fixed 65.421719m-share denominator even though financing that growth may require additional shares.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we had $225.5 million of equity available for issuance under the program.
audit_findings.explanation: There is no demonstrated present denominator error because the supplied denominator covers identified awards, reserves, and forward shares. The remaining ATM capacity concerns future issuance, and its effect depends on issue price, proceeds invested, financing mix, and returns earned. Ignoring future equity while crediting existing holders with all resulting growth could overstate their per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Prepare annual financing schedules for the base and bull capital programs showing operating cash, debt, equity proceeds, issuance prices, incremental shares, and incremental OE; rerun per-share values with year-specific dilution if equity issuance is required.

audit_findings.title: Recurring asset-removal cash costs may be omitted from maintenance capital
audit_findings.magnitude: Asset-removal cash costs were $52.268m in 2025, $58.952m in 2024, and $62.023m in 2023; the 2025 amount equals 20.5% of the $255.5m anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is overstated if D&A is added back and maintenance capital excludes separately reported asset-removal cash expenditures.
audit_findings.evidence: Asset removal costs include expenditures associated with the replacement or retirement of long-lived assets that result from the construction, development, and/or normal use of our assets, primarily our pipeline assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash costs and their recurring nature are demonstrated by the filings, but their inclusion or exclusion in the OE workpaper is unresolved. Their three-year scale is large relative to anchor OE and therefore reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each historical maintenance-capital deduction to conventional capital expenditures plus asset-removal payments, identify any amount already captured elsewhere, and rerun the anchor and scenarios for any net omission.

audit_findings.title: Regulatory accounting can defer cash costs outside earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Net regulatory-asset/liability cash-flow adjustments were +$105.057m in 2025, -$71.475m in 2024, and +$46.118m in 2023, versus $255.5m anchor OE; gross balances at June 30, 2026 were $334.071m of regulatory assets and $457.837m of regulatory liabilities
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash expenditures may be capitalized as regulatory assets instead of reducing earnings, while later recoveries and regulatory liabilities create cash flows with the opposite effect; omitting these movements can distort historical OE and its trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, certain costs that would normally be expensed under GAAP are capitalized or deferred on the balance sheet because it is probable they can be recovered through rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate large, reversing regulatory cash-timing movements, but the supplied record does not identify which additions, recoveries, or refunds were included in OE. Because the annual movements are large relative to anchor OE and can either overstate or understate a particular year's cash economics, the unresolved treatment is materially capable of changing the trend-based valuation.
audit_findings.action: Build a year-by-year roll-forward by regulatory account showing cash additions, earnings deferrals, amortization, customer recoveries or refunds, write-offs, and carrying returns; reconcile each item to OE exactly once and rerun the trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: 2025 pension cost is below the disclosed near-term run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: The disclosed pretax increase is $12.9m ($18.6m estimated for 2026 less $5.7m in 2025), equal to 5.0% of anchor OE; even treating the full pretax increase as a recurring OE reduction implies approximately $181.2m or $2.77 per share below base value
audit_findings.mechanism: A recurring unrecovered pension-cost increase would reduce forecast OE; regulatory recovery or deferral would reduce the shareholder impact.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded net periodic benefit costs for our defined benefit pension plans, prior to regulatory deferrals, of $5.7 million in 2025, and estimate that in 2026, we will record net periodic benefit cost of approximately $18.6 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher run rate is supported by $9.279m of pension cost recorded in the first half of 2026, but the shareholder-borne portion remains unresolved because the company recovers pension costs through regulated rates and recorded regulatory deferrals. Even the conservative assumption that the entire $12.9m pretax increase reduces OE would lower the $54.98 base value to about $52.21 per share, still far below the $79.86 market price; the actual after-tax, unrecovered effect should be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Obtain jurisdiction-level rate recovery and regulatory-deferral schedules, calculate the after-tax amount borne by shareholders, and rerun only if that net amount materially exceeds the disclosed $12.9m pretax increase or combines with other open adjustments.
